recede

/ri-SEED/ — stress on SEED · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To recede is to gradually move back or withdraw from a previous position, becoming more distant over time.

From the stern of the ferry, we watched the island slowly recede into the mist.

Example

As winter approached, the floodwaters slowly receded from the farmland, exposing soggy pastures and leaving behind thick mud.

Recede = re (back — not again!) + cedere (Latin: to go) = to go back. The floodwaters are physically withdrawing and moving backward over time. This is crucial: re- in recede means 'back' in direction, not 'again,' proving that the prefix has two different senses.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

subside: To subside is to sink to a lower, calmer level right where it is — a storm subsides, a fever subsides, an argument subsides. To recede is to move back and away, becoming more distant without necessarily quieting down. Subsiding is a drop in intensity; receding is a growing distance.

ebb: To ebb is to flow back out the way the tide does — falling away for now, often with the sense that it may flow back in again. To recede is to keep drawing back, growing steadily more distant with no promise of return. Tides ebb and come back; a coastline that recedes keeps moving back year after year.

dwindle: To dwindle is to shrink steadily in amount or number — savings dwindle, a crowd dwindles until only a few people remain. To recede is to move back in space, growing more distant rather than smaller. A supply dwindles; a shoreline, a hairline, or a flood recedes.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

advance: move forward toward a position

approach: come nearer and nearer to something

Where it sits · how slowly and completely it fades

back away → withdraw → retreat → recede

back away vs. recede: You back away a step or two from a growling dog, but when floodwaters recede they pull back until they nearly vanish.

withdraw vs. recede: A shy student may withdraw from one conversation, but a memory that recedes slips farther and farther back until it fades from view.

retreat vs. recede: An army may retreat and return the next day, but when a glacier recedes it draws slowly back over many years.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-: back (Latin)

Root — cede: to go (from cedere) (Latin)

Put it together: Watch out — in this word re- means back, not again! Re- (back) + cedere (to go) = 'to go back': to withdraw and grow more distant. Recede is this unit's key reminder that re- has two senses — while restore, resurrect, renaissance, and replenish all use 'again,' recede uses the reversal sense, 'back.'

Use the root in a new word: concede: Rather than argue all night, Maya finally conceded that her brother's route to the lake was shorter.
